مَوَّارٌ , (TA,) or مَوَّارُ المِلَاطِ, (S, TA,) A camel that moves the upper bones of his two arms from side to side; (S, TA;) and مَوَّارُ الضَّبْعَيْنِ [signifies the same]. (A.) ―
-b2- مَوَّارَةٌ, (M, K,) or مَوَّارَةُ اليَدِ, (S, Msb,) A she-camel quick in her pace: (S, Msb:) or easy in her pace, and quick. (M, K.) ―
-b3- رِيحٌ مَوَّارَةٌ Wind that blows the dust to and fro: or that raises the dust: pl. رِيَاحٌ مُورٌ, which is extr. [with respect to rule]. (M.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
